Dinn:
SULTANATE OF DINN

The past century has seen Dinn blossom from a small city-state to a vigorous power spreading outward from the capital in Lamm. As the Sultanate expanded east along the Copper Coast, it brought the teachings of Orthopraxy in its wake, replacing the primitive religion of Delisgar with enlightened right-doing.

Though the Sultanate’s borders have been static for a generation, the ascension of a new sultan has seen a groundswell of popular support for further expansion. The seas to the north and the cities of the south hold great riches, if only they could be shown the wisdom of Orthopraxy. Where the Sultan’s soldiers march, all must give way.
Boonan:
BOONAN FREE STATE

The people of the south have always been fiercely independent, a loose collection of tribes and villages scattered through the mountains and semi-arid lowlands. The Free State was something of a convenient fiction, a nation in name only that came together once a generation to repel military adventures out of Royal Delisgar.

Now, with the Sultanate of Dinn rising to their northeast, the village headmen once again look nervously toward their borders. Many voices in the great Moot now say that the Boonan will never be safe from subjugation until they can plow the seas like the other great powers of the Copper Coast.
Delisgar:
ROYAL DELISGAR

Sprawling Delisgar has dominated the Copper Coast since time immemorial. Once, every knee for two hundred miles bent to the king in Brialgon. Time and decadence have withered the flower of empire, and the word of the throne is not what it once was. Infidel armies press in from the east, and even the Prince of Allakia no longer obeys without question. Nevertheless, the Delisgrene will is not yet broken, and where the royal armies march, the earth shakes.

With the shocking fall of the Diamond Isle to the Sultanate of Dinn, the realm clamors for war. Many holy relics of the Thousand Saints rest in the monasteries of the Isle, and it is unthinkable for infidels to defile them.
Allakia:
PRINCIPALITY OF ALLAKIA

Three hundred years ago, raiders from across the sea pillaged the Copper Coast. They were eventually defeated in battle by Pophanes the Mage, King of Delisgar, but in his wisdom he did not drive them from his shores. Instead, out of respect for their martial might, the king allowed the foreigners to convert to Hagiogy and settle in the west of the empire, a land they named Allakia. Pophanes named his youngest daughter Princess of Allakia, and to this day the principality is ruled by a cadet branch of the blood royal.

The common folk, however, retain their ancestors’ respect for strength. They see the wavering of the Delisgrene throne, and they chafe at the yoke. Why tolerate the rule of an queen who can no longer defend her own borders? Why should not the Prince of Allakia sit on the throne in Brialgon?
